title: 6 Strange Borders, Ending on India's Gifted Island
description:
A countdown of six real borders that look like map mistakes: a German town inside Switzerland, a Spanish town inside France, a road through Canada, and a runway that stops cars. The last one is India's Katchatheevu, an island ceded to Sri Lanka in 1974 that still has a church fishermen sail to.

#borders #katchatheevu #geography

scenes.narration: Your fishing boat from Rameswaram can pass an island that India gave away, with a church Indians still sail to every year.
scenes.headline: India's Gifted Island

scenes.narration: It sounds fake, but that island is real, and it is the strangest of the six borders in this video.
scenes.headline: Six Real Borders

scenes.narration: By the end, you'll see how one tiny rock holds a church, a fishing net and a signature from 1974.
scenes.headline: One Rock, Three Stories

scenes.narration: But first we start in Europe, where a whole town sits inside the wrong country.
scenes.headline: Start In Europe

scenes.narration: Six borders, counted down. Each one is stranger than the last, and the final one belongs to India.
scenes.headline: Countdown Begins

scenes.narration: Stay with me, because every border here is real, and every place I mention you can look up yourself.
scenes.headline: All Of It Is Real

scenes.narration: Number six: Büsingen. Picture a German town with Swiss land on every single side of it.
scenes.headline: Büsingen

scenes.narration: It sits beside the Rhine, wrapped completely by Switzerland, with no German land touching it anywhere.
scenes.headline: Wrapped By Switzerland

scenes.narration: Shops there accept euros and Swiss francs, because the town is part of the Swiss customs area.
scenes.headline: Two Currencies

scenes.narration: Phone numbers follow the Swiss system, yet the cars still wear German number plates.
scenes.headline: Swiss Phones, German Plates

scenes.narration: Residents vote in German elections, yet much of daily life follows Swiss rules.
scenes.headline: German Votes

scenes.narration: A vote in 1918 even asked to join Switzerland, but that never went through.
scenes.headline: The 1918 Vote

scenes.narration: Old deals from centuries ago were never tidied up, so the odd shape just stayed.
scenes.headline: Never Tidied Up

scenes.narration: That is strange. But the next place is a whole town hiding inside France.
scenes.headline: A Town In France

scenes.narration: Number five: Llívia. A Spanish town surrounded by France, and it is there because of one word.
scenes.headline: Llívia

scenes.narration: In 1659, Spain and France signed a treaty that handed France a list of villages in the Pyrenees.
scenes.headline: Treaty Of 1659

scenes.narration: But Llívia counted as a town, not a village, so the treaty's wording left it with Spain.
scenes.headline: Town, Not Village

scenes.narration: On the map, it is a small dot of Spain with the French border looping all the way around it.
scenes.headline: A Dot Of Spain

scenes.narration: A special neutral road links the town to Spain through French land, so locals can still drive home.
scenes.headline: The Neutral Road

scenes.narration: People there speak Catalan, pay in euros, and look out at mountains on every side.
scenes.headline: Catalan In France

scenes.narration: A whole town saved by one word. Next, we cross the Atlantic, where an American road runs through Canada.
scenes.headline: Across The Atlantic

scenes.narration: Number four: Point Roberts. It belongs to Washington state, yet to drive home you must cross into Canada.
scenes.headline: Point Roberts

scenes.narration: In 1846, a treaty drew the border along a straight line, the forty-ninth parallel.
scenes.headline: A Straight Line

scenes.narration: That straight line sliced the tip off a peninsula and left a small American piece stuck to Canada.
scenes.headline: The Sliced Peninsula

scenes.narration: So people in Point Roberts live in the United States, but the only road to the rest of it runs through British Columbia.
scenes.headline: Road Through Canada

scenes.narration: That means passport checks, queues and a drive through another country just to reach the next American town.
scenes.headline: Passports To Go Home

scenes.narration: In 2020, when travel across the border was restricted, this odd shape made life there very hard.
scenes.headline: 2020 Closure

scenes.narration: If that sounds odd, wait until you hear about a corner of Minnesota that is cut off by a lake in Canada.
scenes.headline: Even Stranger Next

scenes.narration: Number three: the Northwest Angle. A corner of Minnesota that sits above the rest of the United States.
scenes.headline: Northwest Angle

scenes.narration: It lies on Lake of the Woods, and by road you can only reach it through Canada.
scenes.headline: Only Via Canada

scenes.narration: The reason is a mapmaking mistake. The 1783 peace treaty relied on a map that got the rivers wrong.
scenes.headline: A Map Mistake

scenes.narration: Later agreements fixed most of the line, but they left this little piece of land on the American side.
scenes.headline: Left Behind

scenes.narration: On the map, it looks like a small notch sticking up into Canada, mostly made of water and forest.
scenes.headline: A Notch In Canada

scenes.narration: If you enjoy strange places like these, subscribe, because new ones are coming every day.
scenes.headline: More Strange Places

scenes.narration: Now for number two, where cars wait at a red light for airplanes.
scenes.headline: Red Light For Planes

scenes.narration: Number two: Gibraltar. A British territory at the tip of Spain, with a road that crosses an airport runway.
scenes.headline: Gibraltar

scenes.narration: The road is called Winston Churchill Avenue, and it cuts straight across the runway.
scenes.headline: Churchill Avenue

scenes.narration: When a plane is about to land or take off, the barriers come down and cars have to stop.
scenes.headline: Barriers Come Down

scenes.narration: So your car waits at a red light for an airplane. Cars stop, planes go.
scenes.headline: Cars Stop, Planes Go

scenes.narration: The runway sits on a narrow strip of land right beside the Spanish border.
scenes.headline: Beside Spain

scenes.narration: It is a real working airport, not a museum, and the road is part of everyday life.
scenes.headline: A Working Airport

scenes.narration: Walk a few minutes and you pass a border, a runway, and the huge Rock of Gibraltar.
scenes.headline: Border, Runway, Rock

scenes.narration: Britain has held Gibraltar since the early 1700s, though Spain still claims it, so this border is argued over.
scenes.headline: Still Argued Over

scenes.narration: Locals treat the waiting planes as normal life. Now the last border is Indian, and it began with one signature in 1974.
scenes.headline: India Is Next

scenes.narration: Number one: Katchatheevu. A tiny island in the Palk Strait, between Rameswaram and Sri Lanka's Delft island.
scenes.headline: Katchatheevu

scenes.narration: It is less than two kilometres long, and no one lives there. There is no drinking water either.
scenes.headline: Nobody Lives There

scenes.narration: Look at where it sits. The Palk Strait is narrow, and fishermen on both sides have shared these waters for ages.
scenes.headline: The Palk Strait

scenes.narration: Tamil fishermen on the Indian side and Tamil fishermen in Sri Lanka speak the same language.
scenes.headline: Same Language

scenes.narration: Yet the island has a church, St Anthony's, built in the early 1900s by a Tamil fisherman named Srinivasa Padaiyachi.
scenes.headline: St Anthony's Church

scenes.narration: St Anthony is the saint of fishermen, so sailors from both sides of the water have prayed there for generations.
scenes.headline: Saint Of Fishermen

scenes.narration: For a long time, the island was linked to the Raja of Ramnad, in what is now Tamil Nadu.
scenes.headline: The Raja Of Ramnad

scenes.narration: Then came 1974. Indira Gandhi's government and Sri Lanka's Sirimavo Bandaranaike signed an agreement drawing the sea border.
scenes.headline: The 1974 Agreement

scenes.narration: That line put Katchatheevu on Sri Lanka's side, so India gave up the island without a shot being fired.
scenes.headline: Given Away

scenes.narration: The agreement even lets Indian fishermen rest there, dry their nets, and visit the church without a visa.
scenes.headline: Nets And No Visa

scenes.narration: Two years later, a 1976 pact said fishing boats from each country must stay out of the other's waters.
scenes.headline: The 1976 Pact

scenes.narration: Here is where the trouble starts. Fish do not read maps, and the sea has no painted line.
scenes.headline: No Line At Sea

scenes.narration: So fishermen from Rameswaram still sail out, cross the line by mistake or need, and meet the Sri Lankan navy.
scenes.headline: Meeting The Navy

scenes.narration: Boats have been seized and fishermen arrested many times, which is why this island keeps coming up in Indian politics.
scenes.headline: Arrests At Sea

scenes.narration: Remember, every other border here changed a road or a currency. This one changes where a fisherman can cast a net.
scenes.headline: Where You Cast A Net

scenes.narration: Many Tamil Nadu leaders have demanded it back, and it became a talking point in the 2024 election.
scenes.headline: Demand To Take It Back

scenes.narration: Sri Lanka says the island is legally its own, so both sides feel strongly about this tiny rock.
scenes.headline: Sri Lanka's Position

scenes.narration: Now the part I promised. Look at what the island is truly famous for, and it is not the border.
scenes.headline: The Real Twist

scenes.narration: Every year in February or March, pilgrims sail to St Anthony's for a weekend of prayer.
scenes.headline: The Annual Festival

scenes.narration: Priests from India and Sri Lanka lead the mass together, and no passport is needed to attend.
scenes.headline: Mass For Two Nations

scenes.narration: So one rock holds a gifted island, a fishing dispute, and a church that two countries share.
scenes.headline: One Rock, Two Nations

scenes.narration: The map can fool you. From Rameswaram it looks like a stepping stone, yet it is Sri Lankan land.
scenes.headline: The Map Fools You

scenes.narration: Let us count them down. Six: Büsingen, a German town wrapped in Switzerland, using two currencies.
scenes.headline: 6: Büsingen

scenes.narration: Five: Llívia, a Spanish town saved inside France by one word in a treaty.
scenes.headline: 5: Llívia

scenes.narration: Four: Point Roberts, where Americans must drive through Canada to get home.
scenes.headline: 4: Point Roberts

scenes.narration: Three: the Northwest Angle, a piece of Minnesota left behind by a bad map.
scenes.headline: 3: Northwest Angle

scenes.narration: Two: Gibraltar, where cars stop at a red light for airplanes.
scenes.headline: 2: Gibraltar

scenes.narration: One: Katchatheevu, an island India gave away, with a church people from both countries still sail to.
scenes.headline: 1: Katchatheevu

scenes.narration: So the next time a map looks simple, remember that a boat from Rameswaram can pass an island India gave away.
scenes.headline: Maps Aren't Simple

scenes.narration: Tomorrow: another place where one small step changes the country you stand in.
scenes.headline: Tomorrow: One Step
